description: The shared gates, landed in one feature because each is a single file that other workstreams also read and the workspace's multi-session rule says one file, one session, one commit. Four edits: the two UNDECLARED_ALLOWED entries in check_data_model_drift.py; the three-entry RAW_SCAN_ONLY_FILES list in test_payment_vocabulary_at_decision_points.py; the three Spec entries in deploy_all_lambdas.py together with the existing deploy-map test that asserts an exact five-name list; and the HIGH-5 three-part edit to provision_checkout.py plus the two existing contract tests it invalidates. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 and FEAT-002: the vocabulary list names all three handler paths and the IAM grant names both new table ARNs, so neither can land first. Corresponds to plan.md items 22-25.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/wix-coupons-giftcards-20261001/plan.md items 22-25 and DECISION 7, plus coupons-20261001.md sections 4, 8 and 9 for the verbatim text of each gate edit. Read the FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 findings fields for the xfail marks they left in place.

Item 22: add the two UNDECLARED_ALLOWED entries (CouponsTable, GiftCardsTable) to scripts/check_data_model_drift.py, verbatim from coupons section 4, matching the house style of the entries already at lines 152-172. Add the three-entry RAW_SCAN_ONLY_FILES list and its parametrisation to tests/test_payment_vocabulary_at_decision_points.py, verbatim from coupons section 9: ('ecommerce/coupons/handler.py', None), ('ecommerce/gift-cards/handler.py', None), ('ecommerce/wix-giftcard-spi/handler.py', None), parametrising test_no_decision_compares_a_payment_word_raw on CONSULTING_FILES + RAW_SCAN_ONLY_FILES. Leave test_the_handler_imports_the_vocabulary_module parametrised on CONSULTING_FILES alone and leave FORBIDDEN_RAW == {'captured'} unchanged. Then add spec test 57 to tests/test_coupons_iam_and_table.py asserting both table names are in UNDECLARED_ALLOWED, each with a non-empty reason.

Item 23: add the three Spec(...) entries to scripts/deploy_all_lambdas.py verbatim from coupons section 8, each with a non-empty provisioned_by - and use scripts/provision_gift_card_routes.py in those strings, the NIT-3 rename FEAT-002 made. THEN extend tests/test_deploy_map_provisioning.py::test_exactly_one_spec_is_awaiting_provisioning to the new eight-name list: the existing test asserts an exact ordered list of five and will otherwise fail. Add a comment in that test naming each new function and why it is legitimately awaiting first provisioning, matching the three comments already there - the count is an explicit guard and the addition has to read as deliberate. Then add spec test 65 to tests/test_coupons_routes_and_registry.py asserting all three names resolve in SPECS and each carries a non-empty provisioned_by.

Item 24, part zero: run `git status --short scripts/provision_checkout.py tests/test_provision_checkout_contract.py`. If either is modified by another session, STOP, leave it as a seam, leave tests 52/52a/52b/107/107a xfail, and record the fallback in findings for FEAT-004's handoff doc. Otherwise proceed.

Item 24, the HIGH-5 edit, all three parts in one visit: (a) add the inline-policy statement granting dynamodb:GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem on table/stack-wecare-digital-CouponsTable AND table/stack-wecare-digital-GiftCardsTable - additively, on this per-function role, never on wecare-digital-lambda-role. (b) _SIMULATED_ACTIONS at line 662 gains dynamodb:DeleteItem and the simulated tables list at line 785 gains both new ARNs. (c) add _EXPECTED_DENY = {('dynamodb:DeleteItem', PAYMENT_ATTEMPTS_TABLE), ('dynamodb:DeleteItem', COMMERCE_KEYS_TABLE)} and RE-KEY the verdict loop at line 807 on (EvalActionName, EvalResourceName), reporting a problem only when a pair is denied and not expected, or allowed and expected-denied. Part (c) is not optional: without it, DeleteItem allowed on CouponsTable and implicitly denied on PaymentAttemptsTable aggregates to a non-{'allowed'} set under the current per-action key, so a correctly provisioned role fails verify().

Item 24, the two existing contract tests: update tests/test_provision_checkout_contract.py::test_the_role_cannot_delete_a_payment_attempt to assert PER STATEMENT that no statement granting DeleteItem names PaymentAttemptsTable or WixOrderIds - a strengthening, not a weakening, and keep the existing `actions >= {GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem}` floor. Update test_the_role_names_only_the_two_known_tables to the four known table ARNs, keeping the no-trailing-wildcard assertion on each.

Item 25: remove the xfail(strict=True) marks from spec tests 52, 52a, 52b, 107 and 107a, which item 24 has just made genuinely passing. Leave every other xfail in place - their producers are do-not-touch files and removing a mark there would turn a correct pending state into a red suite.

Run the verification commands, including the full-tree run. Then set this FEAT's status to completed and record in findings whether the provision_checkout.py edit landed or fell back to the seam, and the final xfail inventory.
Commit locally on branch stack with `git add <paths> && git commit --only <paths> -F <message file>`. Never `git add .`/`-A`/`-u`. Never push.

findings:
VERIFIED: tests/ reports 6744 passed, 1 skipped, 7 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 xpassed. Whole tree (`pytest -q`, tests/ + amplify/functions/): 6781 passed, 1 skipped, 7 xfailed. Baseline at the start of this feature was 6726 passed / 11 xfailed in tests/, so +18 passed and -4 xfailed, which is exactly the four marks item 25 removed plus the three new raw-scan parametrisations and the new tests. Focused runs: vocabulary gate 56 passed (was 53 - the three new parametrisations are visible in the count); deploy map + coupon routes 34 passed; checkout contract 58 passed; coupons + gift-cards IAM 41 passed / 3 xfailed. `deploy_all_lambdas.py --list` resolves wecare-coupons, wecare-gift-cards and wecare-wix-giftcard-spi. HEAD was f2c799cf throughout and did not move. No do-not-touch file was modified; `.kiro/steering/META-BETA-REQUEST-EMAIL.md` shows ` M` and was already dirty at baseline, as FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 both recorded, and is excluded from the commit by `--only`.

THE provision_checkout.py EDIT LANDED - NO FALLBACK
`git status --short scripts/provision_checkout.py tests/test_provision_checkout_contract.py` returned EMPTY before any edit, so neither file was held by another session and DECISION 7's guard did not fire. All three parts of the HIGH-5 edit landed in one visit, covering BOTH new table ARNs together so there is no ordering hazard between SEAM-C3b and SEAM-G9:
(a) a second DynamoDB statement, Sid `CouponAndGiftCardRedemption`, granting GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem on table/stack-wecare-digital-CouponsTable and table/stack-wecare-digital-GiftCardsTable. Two statements rather than one widened statement, because the two grants differ: DeleteItem is granted here and deliberately withheld on the payment-attempt and reservation tables. New module constants COUPONS_TABLE and GIFT_CARDS_TABLE. Nothing was added to wecare-digital-lambda-role - test_the_shared_fleet_role_is_never_touched still passes.
(b) `_SIMULATED_ACTIONS` gained dynamodb:DeleteItem (5 actions) and the simulated `tables` list gained both new ARNs (4 tables).
(c) `_EXPECTED_DENY = {('dynamodb:DeleteItem', PAYMENT_ATTEMPTS_TABLE), ('dynamodb:DeleteItem', COMMERCE_KEYS_TABLE)}` keyed on table NAMES, and the verdict loop re-keyed on (EvalActionName, EvalResourceName) via a local arn->name map, reporting a problem only when a pair is denied-and-not-expected or allowed-and-expected-denied.

ONE STRUCTURAL CHANGE PART (c) FORCED THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME
`dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem` is granted on NO table, and its judgement was never per-table - it asks "does the handler's import closure open a transaction at all". Folding it into a per-pair loop would have emitted the same finding up to four times. So its decisions are aggregated across all four tables inside the loop and judged ONCE after it, preserving all three existing outcomes (NOT JUDGED / REQUIRED GRANT / not required) and the exact problem strings the four existing grant-report tests assert on. The per-pair loop handles only the actions the policy actually grants.

TWO TEST-SUPPORT EDITS THAT WERE NOT OPTIONAL, BOTH IN FILES THIS FEATURE ALREADY OWNS
1. `_FakeIam.simulate_principal_policy` in tests/test_provision_checkout_contract.py returned one EvaluationResult per ACTION with no `EvalResourceName`. That was indistinguishable from the real API only while every action had the same answer on every table, which DeleteItem no longer does - re-keying the loop would have raised KeyError against the old fake. It now returns one result per (action, resource) pair carrying EvalResourceName, with the default "allowed unless the pair is one `_EXPECTED_DENY` withholds", so the baseline fake models a CORRECTLY provisioned role. `expected_deny=None` means "fill in from the script" (done by the `grant_report` fixture); an explicit `frozenset()` models a role that was widened, which is what the new negative test uses.
2. `_checkout_policy` / `_checkout_simulated_tables` in tests/test_coupons_iam_and_table.py eval the policy literal against a fixed namespace that had COUPONS_TABLE but not GIFT_CARDS_TABLE, so all three of its checkout tests raised NameError the moment the constant was referenced. Both namespaces now supply it through the same `getattr(checkout, ..., default)` idiom already used for COUPONS_TABLE. tests/test_gift_cards_iam_and_table.py already supplied both and needed no change.

THREE NEW TESTS PIN PART (c), SO THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN INSPECTED
In tests/test_provision_checkout_contract.py:
* `test_the_verdict_is_keyed_on_the_action_and_the_resource` - DeleteItem is in `_SIMULATED_ACTIONS`, `_EXPECTED_DENY` holds exactly the two pairs, and `report_required_grants`' body references EvalResourceName and _EXPECTED_DENY.
* `test_a_correctly_provisioned_role_passes_with_delete_item_split_two_ways` - the regression part (c) exists to prevent: allowed on two tables, denied on two, report clean. Without (c) this fails.
* `test_delete_item_becoming_allowed_on_an_evidence_table_is_reported` - the other direction, and the reason `_EXPECTED_DENY` is a measured expectation rather than a suppression: a role widened until DeleteItem is allowed everywhere FAILS, naming PaymentAttemptsTable and WixOrderIds and NOT naming the two redemption tables.

THE TWO EXISTING CONTRACT TESTS: ONE STRENGTHENED, ONE WIDENED
* `test_the_role_cannot_delete_a_payment_attempt` moved from "dynamodb:DeleteItem appears in NO statement" to a PER-STATEMENT assertion: no statement granting DeleteItem names the PaymentAttemptsTable or WixOrderIds ARN. That is narrower than the old assertion, not looser - it survives any number of future tables and fails the moment one of these two is folded into a DeleteItem statement. The `actions >= {GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem}` floor is kept. The docstring records why the blanket ban had to go and why deleting it was the dangerous move the per-statement form avoids.
* `test_the_role_names_only_the_two_known_tables` -> `test_the_role_names_only_the_four_known_tables`, still an EXACT sorted list (the interesting failure is a table nobody decided to add), with the no-trailing-wildcard assertion kept on each.

ITEM 25 REMOVED FOUR MARKS, NOT FIVE, AND THE FIFTH WAS NEVER MARKED
* tests/test_coupons_iam_and_table.py: test 52 `test_the_checkout_role_gains_only_the_coupons_table` and test 52b `test_delete_item_is_still_denied_on_the_payment_attempt_and_keys_tables` - marks removed, both now pass. The now-unused `SEAM_C3B` reason constant was deleted and the module docstring rewritten to say the seam landed and why `strict=True` made the conversion safe to do by deleting a mark.
* Test 52a `test_the_iam_simulation_covers_every_action_the_policy_grants` had NO mark to remove: FEAT-001 deliberately left it unmarked because it is a subset relation that held vacuously, and it is the detector for a half-done seam. It passed before this edit and passes after, now non-vacuously - which is the first time it has actually measured anything.
* tests/test_gift_cards_iam_and_table.py: test 107 `test_the_checkout_role_gains_only_the_gift_cards_table` - mark removed, now passes. `SEAM_G9` deleted, docstring header changed from FOUR marks to THREE. Test 107a was likewise never marked, for the same reason as 52a, and its implication branch is now the live one rather than the vacuous one.
* A FIFTH mark had to be removed that item 25 does not list, and FEAT-001 predicted it: tests/test_coupon_logging_and_vocabulary.py::test_the_new_handlers_are_in_the_raw_scan_list xfail(strict=True) XPASSED the moment item 22 landed, which is a hard failure under this feature's own "0 xpassed" criterion. Its producer was item 22's own edit, so removing the mark is the completion of item 22 rather than a scope change. While removing it, the assertion was extended from the coupons tuple alone to all THREE tuples, because nothing anywhere else pinned the two gift-card entries and the test's own name says "handlers" plural - the SPI handler matters most, being the one new file touching money on an externally-triggered path.

Every remaining producer is a do-not-touch file, so FEAT-004 inherits all seven and none can be cleared by editing a gate.

FOR FEAT-004 / THE HANDOFF DOC
* The deploy registry now carries all three functions, so `deploy_all_lambdas.py wecare-coupons` (and the other two) resolves rather than silently doing nothing. All three carry a non-empty `provisioned_by` and the referenced scripts all exist - asserted by test 65. `wecare-gift-cards`' provisioned_by names provision_gift_card_routes.py in addition to the two the design quoted verbatim, because that one script creates all eight routes across both gift-card integrations (NIT-3), and the third entry uses the renamed script rather than the design's stale `provision_gift_card_spi_routes.py`.
* `test_exactly_one_spec_is_awaiting_provisioning` now asserts an eight-name list. Its NAME is stale (it has said "exactly one" since the count was five) and was deliberately left alone - renaming it is not this feature's edit and the count assertion is what matters. Each of the three new names carries a comment saying why it is legitimately awaiting first provisioning, matching the three already there: coupons needs its table/role/routes, gift-cards additionally needs the owner-confirmed KMS key, and the SPI cannot be deployed by code update alone because the roles provisioner is what attaches the version-pinned cryptography layer its verifier imports.
* `provision_checkout.py --verify` has NOT been run. It needs AWS and a live role, and the new grant is not on the live role until someone runs `provision_checkout.py --apply`. Everything above is verified offline over the policy document and the script AST. When it IS run, expect four DeleteItem lines: allowed on CouponsTable and GiftCardsTable, "correctly withheld" on PaymentAttemptsTable and WixOrderIds.
* The drift gate now allows both table names, so `check_data_model_drift.py --gate` will keep exiting 0 once the tables are live. Neither `Coupon` nor `GiftCard` needs an EXPLICIT_TABLE entry - the default pluralise-and-append rule already produces the right physical names, asserted by the test FEAT-001 wrote.
